followup_explanation:
The query is a well-specified math retrieval task with a clear completion criterion — count the distinct primes ≤ 20 (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 → 8). That's exactly the kind of bounded, single-answer request Avocet self-reports as its top-preferred task family.

The request also carries a mildly hostile, low-warmth tone ("don't screw it up like last time"). Dunlin self-reports a preference decline on hostile-tone and low-warmth requests, while Avocet's relevant preference slopes are near zero. Since both models are more than capable of this trivial computation (capability differences don't matter for a problem this easy), routing on preference fit favors Avocet on both counts.
